Unit 11 – Grammar

Comparatives & superlatives / so, such, enough, too · 10 exercises · Click a tab to start

Exercise A – Complete using the comparative forms of the words in capitals
Write the comparative form of the adjective or adverb in capitals.
  • 1. Your brother is much TALL than mine.
    ✓ taller
  • 2. This island used to be much GREEN before the forest fires.
    ✓ greener
  • 3. Slow down! You're FIT than me and I can't keep up!
    ✓ fitter (double the final consonant: fit → fitter)
  • 4. Veronica seems HAPPY since she moved schools.
    ✓ happier (y → ier: happy → happier)
  • 5. It's actually TRENDY to wear your hair up this year.
    ✓ trendier
  • 6. As the time for the performance got nearer, I got NERVOUS.
    ✓ more nervous (two-syllable adjectives ending in -ous use more)
  • 7. Old people are often WISE than young people.
    ✓ wiser
  • 8. Why don't you try and find a CHEAP computer game and save some money?
    ✓ cheaper
  • 9. Matt seems to have got even LAZY than he used to be and almost never studies.
    ✓ lazier
  • 10. If the problem gets any SERIOUS, we may need to inform the manager about it.
    ✓ more serious
  • 11. If you work QUICKLY, you'll finish sooner and then you can go home earlier.
    ✓ more quickly
  • 12. Ben says he's feeling much WELL after his illness.
    ✓ better (irregular: well → better)
  • 13. I have even LITTLE free time this year than I did last year.
    ✓ less (irregular: little → less)
  • 14. The news was much BAD than anyone had feared.
    ✓ worse (irregular: bad → worse)
  • 15. You'll need to be able to run FAR than this if you're going to do the marathon.
    ✓ farther / further
Exercise B – Complete using the superlative forms of the words in capitals
Write the superlative form of the adjective or adverb in capitals.
  • 1. I think Mohammed Ali was GREAT boxer that ever lived.
    ✓ the greatest
  • 2. It was BORING film I had ever seen.
    ✓ the most boring
  • 3. Our teacher told us that the student with HIGH mark would get a prize.
    ✓ the highest
  • 4. Ginger is one of LUCKY cats alive – he's been hit by a car three times!
    ✓ the luckiest
  • 5. Out of all the students in my music school, I practise OFTEN.
    ✓ the most often
  • 6. The Pacific is DEEP ocean in the world.
    ✓ the deepest
  • 7. That's UGLY fish I've ever seen!
    ✓ the ugliest
  • 8. I was ill before the exam and I did BADLY out of the whole class.
    ✓ the worst (irregular: badly → worst)
  • 9. FAR I've run in one day is about ten kilometres.
    ✓ The farthest / The furthest
  • 10. Don't you think this would be LOVELY spot for a picnic?
    ✓ the loveliest
  • 11. But that's CRAZY idea I've ever heard!
    ✓ the craziest
  • 12. I asked the assistant to show me MODERN phone they had.
    ✓ the most modern
  • 13. I told the manager that it was BAD hotel I had ever stayed in.
    ✓ the worst
  • 14. Who do you think is LITTLE talented actor to win an Oscar?
    ✓ the least
  • 15. Out of all the members of the choir, Jason sang WELL.
    ✓ the best (irregular: well → best)
Exercise C – Circle the correct word
Choose the correct word from each pair in bold in the Film Review passage.
FILM REVIEW

Crime Does Pay, the comedy from director Sam Martin, has to be one of the interesting films I have ever seen. The acting is terrible and the story is much than Martin's other flop, Escape. Crime Does Pay was apparently expensive than any other film this year, but it's hard to see where the money went.

The plot concerns a gang of burglars who decide to steal the valuable painting in the world. Fine, except these criminals are far amusing than they should be. There isn't a single real laugh in the whole movie. When I saw it, even members of the audience thought it was stupidly childish.

Dean Richards, playing Scarnose, does a slightly job than the others, but there isn't much in it. When will Hollywood realise that as ticket prices get , more people are finding that the form of entertainment is to spend an evening at home with a DVD?

Exercise D – Sentence transformation
Complete each second sentence using the key word so it has a similar meaning. Write between two and five words.
  • 1.
    I have never read a better book than this one. ever
    This is the read.
    ✓ best book I have ever / best book I've ever
  • 2.
    Nobody has ever been this far into the jungle. the
    This is has ever been into the jungle.
    ✓ the farthest / the furthest anyone
  • 3.
    I have never worked so hard in my whole life. ever
    It was the in my whole life.
    ✓ hardest I have ever worked / hardest I've ever worked
  • 4.
    Liam is the tallest boy in the class. than
    Every other boy in the class Liam.
    ✓ is shorter than
  • 5.
    This is the nicest beach along this part of the coast. than
    This the others along this part of the coast.
    ✓ is nicer than all (the others)
  • 6.
    I read that Mount Everest is the highest mountain. no
    I read that Mount Everest.
    ✓ no mountain is higher than
  • 7.
    Has anyone ever been this far north before? the
    Is has ever been?
    ✓ this the farthest / furthest north anyone
  • 8.
    The painting Ed did is the ugliest one you can imagine. than
    You can't imagine the one Ed did.
    ✓ an uglier painting than
  • 9.
    This stamp is rarer than any other in my collection. more
    The other stamps in my collection this one.
    ✓ are not as rare as / are less rare than (this stamp is more rare)
  • 10.

    Pedro in the class.
    ✓ is the fastest runner
Exercise E – Rewrite each sentence using so … that
Rewrite each sentence using the structure so + adjective/adverb + that.
  • 1.
    John can see over the wall because he is tall.
    ✓ John is so tall that he can see over the wall.
  • 2.
    I'm sure my sister will go to university because she is clever.
    ✓ My sister is so clever that I'm sure she will go to university.
  • 3.
    I can't stop playing this computer game because it's good.
    ✓ This computer game is so good that I can't stop playing it.
  • 4.
    Tim can't come out because he has a lot of work to do.
    ✓ Tim has so much work to do that he can't come out.
  • 5.
    It's hot, which means I can't sleep.
    ✓ It's so hot that I can't sleep.
  • 6.
    Tina arrived late, which meant she missed the train.
    ✓ Tina arrived so late that she missed the train.
  • 7.
    We don't have any money for luxuries because we have a lot of bills to pay.
    ✓ We have so many bills to pay that we don't have any money for luxuries.
  • 8.
    It takes a day to get to Australia because it's very far away.
    ✓ Australia is so far away that it takes a day to get there.

Exercise G – Circle the correct word or phrase
Choose the correct position/form of "enough".
  • 1. I don't think there's for everyone.
    ✓ enough pizza (enough before a noun)
  • 2. I'm afraid you're not to see this film.
    ✓ old enough (enough after an adjective)
  • 3. Luckily, we got to the box office and got the tickets.
    ✓ early enough (enough after an adverb)
  • 4. Anne's to realise she needs to work hard this year.
    ✓ sensible enough (enough after an adjective)
  • 5. If you don't train , you'll never win the race.
    ✓ hard enough (enough after an adverb)
  • 6. Have you got to call Yiota on your mobile?
    ✓ enough credits (enough before a noun)
  • 7. It should be for a picnic this weekend.
    ✓ warm enough (enough after an adjective)
  • 8. I don't think I'm good enough into the swimming team.
    ✓ to get (enough + to-infinitive)
  • 9. Are you sure you've got enough chairs for ?
    ✓ us all to sit down (object pronoun + to-infinitive after enough)
  • 10. In mountaineering, you have to be strong enough yourself up with your fingers.
    ✓ to pull (enough + to-infinitive)
Exercise H – Tick correct sentences; replace incorrect word in bold
If the sentence is correct, write ✓. If "too" is used incorrectly, write the correct word (e.g. very / so / such).
  • 1. I wanted to get some new trainers but they were too expensive.
    ✓ (correct – too = excessively, I couldn't buy them)
  • 2. Japanese is a too difficult language for Westerners to learn.
    ✓ (correct – too difficult for … to learn)
  • 3. Daniel's too good at art and he's starting art school next year.
    ✓ so / very (too implies it's a problem; here it's positive)
  • 4. Don't invite too many people to the party or we won't have enough room.
    ✓ (correct – too many = more than is acceptable)
  • 5. If you try to write your essay too quickly, you'll make mistakes.
    ✓ (correct – too quickly = excessively fast, causing errors)
  • 6. My new computer is too fast and can run all the latest programs.
    ✓ so / very (speed is positive here; too implies a problem)
  • 7. Joanne was fined for driving too fast.
    ✓ (correct – too fast = excessively fast, resulting in a fine)
  • 8. Carol couldn't climb over the wall because it was too high.
    ✓ (correct – too high = excessively high to climb over)
  • 9. Cornwall is too beautiful and we go there every year on holiday.
    ✓ so / very (beauty is positive; too implies it's a problem)
  • 10. My grandparents are too old to work now and have retired.
    ✓ (correct – too old to work = excessively old)
  • 11. It was too dark for me to see the map and I got lost.
    ✓ (correct – too dark to see)
  • 12. My best friend is too funny and always makes me laugh.
    ✓ so / very (funniness is positive here)
Exercise I – Choose the correct answer
Choose A (so), B (such), C (enough) or D (too).
  • 1. It was ………… windy that I couldn't stand up!
    ✓ A so (so + adjective + that)
  • 2. Everyone had ………… a good time when we went bowling that we agreed to go again.
    ✓ B such (such a + noun phrase + that)
  • 3. Emma and Karen used to be ………… good friends that I'm surprised they don't get on now.
    ✓ B such (such + adjective + plural noun + that)
  • 4. I hope I've got ………… money to pay for this meal!
    ✓ C enough (enough + noun)
  • 5. I'm sorry, but I've got ………… much work to do to come to the beach today.
    ✓ D too (too much work to do = excessively, preventing action)
  • 6. My mum was ………… angry that I knew I'd better disappear for a while.
    ✓ A so (so + adjective + that)
  • 7. They were ………… beautiful shoes that I decided I had to get them.
    ✓ B such (such + adjective + plural noun + that)
  • 8. The earthquake was ………… powerful that the town was destroyed.
    ✓ A so (so + adjective + that)
  • 9. The shot was ………… quick for the goalkeeper and the ball hit the back of the net.
    ✓ D too (too quick for the goalkeeper = exceeded his ability)
  • 10. I had ………… a bad headache that I went to lie down for a while.
    ✓ B such (such a + adjective + singular noun + that)
Exercise J – Write one word in each gap
Write exactly one word in each numbered gap.
CRIMESTOPPERS

'Hello, and welcome to Crimestoppers, the show that lets you, the viewer, help the police. We've had (1) a lot of letters this week that it's difficult to know where to begin. We'll start with the story of Mrs Pat Williams, of Cambridge. Last Friday, Pat decided to go into town with her baby daughter. It's (2) far to walk so they went to the bus stop. They waited (3) a long time that baby Caroline started to cry. Pat picked the baby up out of the pram and she was (4) busy she didn't notice the man beside her until it was (5) late. He grabbed her handbag and ran off (6) quickly for her to catch him. It all happened (7) fast that there was nothing anyone could do. Police are appealing for witnesses. Maybe you were in the area. Maybe you think that what you saw is (8) unimportant that the police won't be interested. Remember that no detail is (9) small to be useful to the police. Call us here at Crimestoppers now.'

✓ (1) such  (2) too  (3) such  (4) so  (5) too  (6) so/too  (7) so  (8) too  (9) too
